To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
data journalists do not fully implement the ethical notions of openness and accountability.
data journalists are aware of ethical standards and that they try to apply them in their daily work.
data journalism is indeed a practice that reflects many of the ethical principles of the open source community.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how data journalism can be understood as an ethical practice in the sense of a culture of open access, and how the ethical standards of data journalism are reflected in the everyday work of data journalists.

the question whether data journalists are aware of and actively implement the ethical principles of open source in their work routines and what the implications of such practices are for the quality and credibility of data journalism.
the question whether and how data journalism can effectively implement the normative principles of the open source movement in its everyday work routine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
data journalists have a strong ethical responsibility to be open and transparent about the data they are working on and to provide their audience with the means to scrutinize their work.
open source is a powerful and promising approach for the ethical practice of data journalism, but that it is not yet sufficiently implemented.
data journalists are indeed aware of the ethical challenges that open source implies and that they are able to deal with them in their everyday work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
data journalism is indeed deeply rooted in the culture of open source, which comes along with a high degree of transparency, shareability, and accountability.

the ethical challenges of data journalism are not only related to the question of whether and how to implement the open source culture but that the ethical challenges are even more related to the question how to balance the open source culture with the traditional journalistic values of objectivity and balance.
data journalists are not yet fully aware of the ethical issues that arise from the implementation of open source principles.
The main takeaway from our work is that

data journalists have to deal with a number of ethical challenges that are not necessarily related to their work with data but to the way they interact with their audience and the way their audience interact with each other.

data journalism can be considered a practice that is strongly embedded in the ethical notions of open source and that data journalists are very aware of the importance of ethical principles and best practices.

while the open source movement and the open source culture are deeply rooted in the data journalism community and its ethical standards, the ethical challenges data journalists are facing in their everyday work are still not sufficiently reflected in research and in practice.
